newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: London robustas tipped to fall US$30-$100 - trade.
newsitem.headline: London robustas tipped to fall US$30-$100 - trade.

text.p: London robusta futures are expected to open up to US$100 lower later on Tuesday, but Far East coffee dealers said a fall of $30-$50 seems more likely.
"London should continue going down by about $30-$40," a coffee dealer for a U.S. commodity company said. "The funds are basically liquidating their positions."
"It should be $100 lower, but it seems more likely that it will fall by only $30-$50. It's following New York's lead," another dealer said.

Coffee prices have dived in a savage correction with the July futures contract in New York, slipping 22.45 U.S. cents on the day to end on Monday at 253.95 cents/lb, down about 20 percent from the 20-year peak last Thursday of 318 cents.
LIFFE's July coffee contract sank on Monday, free-falling $355 to end yesterday at $2,115, just off the day's low of $2,100 a tonne.
"It did not make sense to see the (arabica) market at three dollars a pound. The more reasonable level would be at 200-230 cents," a dealer said.
One dealer forecast that if London robustas break $2,100, "we'll probably see the market go all the way down to $2,000. This correction was expected, but they did not expect it to be so drastic."
The Asian coffee business was quiet as exporters stayed on the sidelines waiting for the dust in New York and London to settle.
"It's a very confusing market," one dealer said.
Indonesia's benchmark Grade 4 coffee, 80 defects, was quoted by the trade at around $1,865/875 a tonne FOB Lampung, down from a peak last week of around $2,200/300 a tonne on the same basis.
Vietnam's Grade 2 coffee, 8.0 percent black and broken, was seen by the trade at $1,895/915 a tonne FOB Saigon, against the peak last week of about $2,250 a tonne on the same basis.
